title: Most people who played Metroid in 1986 never actually saw its most famous moment.
description:
Most people who played Metroid in 1986 never actually saw its most famous moment.

Samus Aran is called 'he' throughout Metroid's instruction manual, which also admits that little is known about 'him'. That was not a translation error. Nintendo built the disguise into the game's own paperwork.

Metroid's ending depends on how long it takes to finish. Only the fastest clears show Samus without her suit at all. A first playthrough drawn out on paper by hand, the only option in 1986, realistically took five to ten hours. That ending does not remove her helmet.

Clear the game inside that and the ending swaps Samus's armour for a bikini instead.

Producer, working with director Satoru Okada, on a game that helped invent the exploration genre later named after it: the metroidvania.

Sources:
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metroid_(video_game) - read in full: confirms director Satoru Okada, producer Gunpei Yokoi, and artists including Hiroji Kiyotake, Hirofumi Matsuoka and Yoshio Sakamoto; release dates of 6 August 1986 for the Japanese Famicom Disk System version and August 1987 for the North American NES version; and that the game shows one of five endings based on completion time, with only the third, fourth and fifth endings showing Samus Aran without her suit.
- https://waltoriouswritesaboutgames.com/2021/10/20/history-lessons-metroid/ - a full playthrough account, read in full: confirms the instruction manual calls Samus 'he' throughout while admitting little is known about 'him'; that a realistic first playthrough of five to ten hours, mapped out by hand, produces an ending where Samus does not remove her helmet at all; and that clearing the game in under an hour, which the author cross checked against a Metroid wiki endings list, gives an ending where Samus wears a bikini instead of her armour.
